info.title: MonitorFlow public API
info.description: Scripts and integrations use `/api/v1` with an API key made under Admin › API keys: `Authorization: Bearer mfk_…`. A key acts as the administrator who made it, within its reach (everything, a customer or a site), its access and its areas. Lists that can grow take `limit` and `cursor` and answer `next_cursor`, null on the last page. Every error has `error`, plain words, and `code`, stable. Writes may carry `Idempotency-Key`; the same request again within 24 hours gets the first answer with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`. A key makes up to 600 requests a minute; answers carry `RateLimit-Limit`, `RateLimit-Remaining` and `RateLimit-Reset`, and 429 carries `Retry-After`. See ADR-0101.

403.description: The key's role or areas do not allow it: `forbidden` or `api_key_scope`

404.description: Not found, or outside the key's reach: `not_found`

429.description: Over the key's rate limit: `rate_limited`, with `Retry-After`

post.description:
Administrators of what it notifies about. Makes its signing secret
and answers it this once; events start at once. `allow_private` takes
a global administrator. Audited as `integration.create`, with the
URL's host only. Not stored for `Idempotency-Key`, as the answer holds
the secret: a retry with the same key answers 409 `conflict`, saying
it was done; list the integrations to find it, and renew its secret if
it was lost.

parameters.description: 1 to 255 visible ASCII characters, a UUID usually. The same request again within 24 hours gets the first answer instead of running twice.

put.description:
Replaces its name, URL, events, what it notifies about and
`allow_private`. Administrators of what it notifies about now and of
what it will. A `url` left empty keeps the stored one. Another URL
gets a new signing secret, answered this once, so the old secret never
signs for another receiver; the old one stops at once. Anyone but a
global administrator keeps `allow_private` only with the same URL.
Audited as `integration.update`. Safe to repeat; with
`Idempotency-Key`, the answer is kept 24 hours, a new secret included.

post.description:
Queues one event, by `event_id`, or every event from `from` to `to`
that the integration asks for and notifies about, again, oldest
first, with the same IDs and `X-MonitorFlow-Replay: 1`. Events are
kept 30 days. They go out while the integration is on. Administrators
of what it notifies about. Audited as `integration.replay`. Not safe
to repeat: each call queues them again; send `Idempotency-Key` to
retry.

post.summary: Pause or turn on an integration
post.description:
`paused` stops new events for it; deliveries already queued wait. `on`
resumes a paused or turned off one, and its day of failures starts
again: what it missed while not on is not queued, so send it again
with the replay. Administrators of what it notifies about. Audited as
`integration.state`. Safe to repeat.

incident_ids.description: 1 to [`MAX_LIMIT`] incidents, like a group of a notification.

Acknowledged.description:
Body of the answer: the incidents this request acknowledged. The
others were resolved, or someone acknowledged them first.

Aggregation.description: A simple aggregation across the selected series.

AiCommandsChange.description: The last `ai_commands` command of a server, in `GET /api/servers/{id}`.

requested_by.description: The username, `null` when the account is gone.

command.description: Runs this instead of the proposal, recorded as an `edit`.

CommandDetail.description:
`GET /api/commands/{id}`: the command and its output, each at most
the last 64 KiB.

health_timeout_s.description:
`self_update`: seconds the new agent has to connect before the
old one comes back; 30 to 3600, 300 by default.

packages.description: Packages to upgrade; empty or absent for all.

ttl_s.description:
Seconds the agent may still start it; [`MIN_TTL_S`] to
[`MAX_TTL_S`], default [`DEFAULT_TTL_S`].

parameters.description: The payload as JSON, for kinds the API knows.

site_count.description: Sites of the customer the user reads, not all of them.

command.description: What will run, or what was rejected.

details.description:
For instance `{"reason": "threshold_removed"}`, `{"notified":
true}` when a silence ended, `{"username", "via"}` when
acknowledged, or `{"step", "steps", "minutes", "told"}` for a
follow-up step.

kind.description:
`opened`, `escalated`, `deescalated`, `resolved`, what a silence
did: `silenced` and `silence_ended` (ADR-0079), `acknowledged`, and
`followed_up` when a follow-up step told someone (ADR-0082).

occurred_at.description: Sample time of the change, or the server clock without a sample.

severity.description: Severity after the change; `null` once resolved.

FollowUpView.description: Where an incident is in its follow-up.

next.description: Who it would tell then, people first; empty when nobody can be.

next_at.description: When the next step is told if nobody acknowledges.

started_at.description: When the first message went out.

state.description:
`waiting` for the next step at `next_at`, `silenced` until a silence
ends then waiting, or `stopped`.

step.description: Steps told so far, and how many there are now.

stop_reason.description:
When stopped: `acknowledged`, `resolved`, `not_critical`, or
`finished` once every step was told.

GroupView.description: A notification that told this incident with others (ADR-0080).

incidents.description:
How many incidents it told that the user may read, this one
included. Members on sites outside the user's scope are not counted.

GuestKind.description: What a Proxmox guest is, which picks its API path.

oneOf.description:
Who is told next if nobody acknowledges (ADR-0082); `null` when no
follow-up started: a warning, or not sent yet.

next_cursor.description: Pass as `cursor` for the next page; `null` on the last one.

IncidentView.description:
One incident. Field names and types are part of the API contract: add
fields, never rename or remove them.

acknowledged_by.description:
Who said they are on it, and when (ADR-0082); `null` until someone
does. The name stays when the account is removed.

can_acknowledge.description:
Whether the reader may acknowledge it: open, not acknowledged, and
the reader an operator or above of its site.

hostname.description: The server's hostname, or the relay's name.

instance.description: `""` for a series without an instance.

metric.description: `offline` when the server or relay stopped reporting (ADR-0072).

opened_at.description: Sample times, not the server clock.

peak_value.description: The worst value seen while open.

relay_id.description: Set for a relay's offline incident only (ADR-0072).

severity.description: `warning` or `critical`; the last one while resolved.

silenced.description: Whether a silence ever held back a notification of it.

silenced_until.description:
While open and covered by a silence, when the last one ends
(ADR-0079).

threshold.description: The threshold as it was when the incident opened.

Integration.description: An endpoint as the web interface shows it; never its secret.

allow_private.description: Whether it may deliver to private and local addresses.

customer_id.description:
The customer it covers, or the customer of the site it covers;
`null` for everything.

events.description: The events it gets, in the order of `events` in the list.

failing_since.description: The first failure since the last success; `null` while it works.

last_error.description:
The most recent failure of a delivery, in plain words; `null`
when none failed.

last_success_at.description: The last delivery it accepted; `null` before the first.

name.description: Tells integrations apart, like the tool it sends to.

origin.description:
The URL's scheme, host and port: its path and query may hold a
token (ADR-0123).

tags.name: notifications
tags.description: Notification channels: where messages to people go when an incident opens, gets worse or ends, a command waits for approval, an update fails, a backup fails or a new version is out. A channel is an email address list sent through a mail server, a webhook, a chat channel (`slack`, `teams`, `discord`) or a plugin's, and notifies about everything, one customer or one site. Only administrators reach channels, and only those of what they administer: everything takes a global administrator (a key with every reach), a customer an administrator of it, a site an administrator of it or of its customer; others answer 404. Secrets are write-only: the mail password, signing secret, chat webhook URL or plugin secret settings go in `secret` and never come back, a channel says only `has_secret`, and a webhook shows only its URL's origin, as its path and query often hold a token. A channel saved by anyone but a global administrator only sends to public addresses. Every change is in the audit log, with the key's ID. API keys need the `alerts` area. For machines rather than people, use an integration.

tags.name: integrations
tags.description: Integrations: another tool, like a PSA or an automation, that gets MonitorFlow's events as one signed JSON `POST` per event: incidents, servers, updates, campaigns and approvals, each integration choosing which. The body follows [`docs/events/v1.schema.json`](https://github.com/Kidoly/monitorflow/blob/main/docs/events/v1.schema.json); the receiver's rules and code to check signatures are in [`docs/integrations.md`](https://github.com/Kidoly/monitorflow/blob/main/docs/integrations.md). In short: each request carries `X-MonitorFlow-Event`, `X-MonitorFlow-Delivery` (the event's `id`), `X-MonitorFlow-Timestamp` and `X-MonitorFlow-Signature`, `sha256=` and the HMAC-SHA256 of `{timestamp}.{raw body}` under the integration's signing secret, plus `X-MonitorFlow-Replay: 1` when sent again. Delivery is at least once: de-duplicate on the `id`. Anything but a 2xx within 15 seconds is retried after 30 seconds, then twice as long each time up to an hour, for 24 hours; an integration that accepts nothing for 24 hours is turned off and administrators are told. Events are kept 30 days and can be sent again with the same IDs. An integration notifies about everything, one customer or one site, and is managed by the administrators of that place, like a notification channel; others get 404. The URL and the signing secret are write-only: answers show the URL's origin, as its path and query often hold a token, and the secret only once, when it is made. Private and local addresses need a global administrator (a key with every reach). Every change is in the audit log, with the key's ID. API keys need the `administration` area.
